note: Dated events during 23 Oct – 1 Nov 2026. Sources, best first: SmartShanghai (/events/<category>/?date=YYYY-MM-DD is date-filterable and is the workhorse, but its cards carry an 'Ongoing' promo block that repeats on every date and whose 'until' strings go stale, so confirm end dates elsewhere); the arts festival's own site, artsbird.com/en/calendar/2026-10, whose page payload carries the full dated programme; Dance Reflections by Van Cleef & Arpels, which co-presents a dance strand inside the festival and publishes exact dates that no general listing carries; english.shanghai.gov.cn, official and English, for its monthly 'exhibitions and performances in <month>' roundups; and the venue primaries (Power Station of Art, Museum of Art Pudong at museumofartpd.org.cn, Fotografiska Shanghai, West Bund Museum at wbmshanghai.com, Rockbund, hiveart.cn, Shanghai Culture Square at shcstheatre.com). Then, for the corners the big listings miss: shanghaiconcerts.com for classical and recitals with venue and date in English; 247tickets.com for English ticketing across stage, music and experiences; SmartShanghai's own periodically-updated Shanghai Jazz Guide for the venue-by-venue jazz roster (JZ, Heyday, the Peace Hotel band, Wooden Box); e-flux.com/announcements, which carries institutional art openings before the local listings do; and shanghaitourism.org's festivals and events calendar for date ranges. Two traps recorded so they are not walked into twice: timeoutshanghai.com is dormant, its content years old; and shanghaijazz.com is a restaurant in Madison, New Jersey, nothing to do with this city. Entries are never deleted by a refresh: a listing that has ended gets "archived": true (plus "archivedOn") and moves into the page's 'Earlier finds' disclosure, so nothing is lost. An entry nobody wanted gets "hidden": true (plus a short "hiddenNote" saying why) and drops into the 'Hidden' disclosure for every reader, not just the one whose browser it was rejected in — that is the difference from the × on a row, which is local to one browser. A refresh must not un-hide one or re-add it as a new entry; a reader who disagrees can restore it on their own copy, which is stored locally and never written back here. `added` drives the New flag for its first 14 days and is never rewritten. `start`/`end` (ISO, either omissible for open-ended runs) place an entry: long runs render under 'Running throughout', short ones slot into the day-by-day calendar on their first in-window day. Optional `weekdays` (e.g. ["Wed","Sat","Sun"]) for recurring patterns, `dates` (ISO list) for specific occurrences, and `closed` (weekday list, e.g. ["Mon"]) restrict which trip days the "Add to a day" picker offers — so a Wednesday-only night can't be pinned to a Tuesday. Absent all three, eligibility is the run intersected with the trip window. Optional `planned` (a day id like "d7") marks a find that is already an itinerary stop on that day: the page then shows "Already on <day>" in place of the picker, since there is nothing to add. Git history holds every past version of this file.

events.title: On Top of the World Tree
events.blurb: Nearly 3,000 artefacts from Mexico, Peru and China, tracing the Olmec, Maya and Inca alongside their Shang and Zhou counterparts. Walking distance from the hotel, closed Mondays; timed tickets via WeChat.
events.archiveNote: End date was off by a year: official sources (Shanghai Museum, Xinhua, PR Newswire) confirm the run is 9 Jul 2026 – 14 Nov 2027, a 16-month show, not closing 14 Nov 2026. Replaced below with a corrected entry — it's open for the whole trip either way.

events.title: On Top of the World Tree
events.blurb: Nearly 3,000 artefacts from Mexico, Peru and China, tracing the Olmec, Maya and Inca alongside their Shang and Zhou counterparts. Walking distance from the hotel, closed Mondays; timed tickets via WeChat. It's a 16-month run through Nov 2027, so it covers the entire trip.

events.title: Reinventing Landscape
events.when: closed 18 Oct, six days before you land
events.blurb: Volume IV of the museum's five-year Pompidou collaboration, around 70 works from the French collection. Three minutes' walk from the Long Museum and Tank Shanghai, both already on the Sunday. Closed Mondays.
events.archiveNote: Run confirmed as 28 Apr 2025 – 18 Oct 2026 against the museum and ticketing listings. It was logged with no end date, so it rendered as running throughout the trip when in fact it shuts six days before arrival. Whatever replaces it in Gallery 1 & 2 is worth a look closer to the date.

events.title: Sleep No More
events.blurb: Punchdrunk's masked-audience immersive theatre, in its permanent Shanghai run. Daily except Monday and Tuesday, three-plus hours, entirely solo-friendly by design. Book ahead via SmartTicket or the venue.
events.archiveNote: The Shanghai production has ended. Its final performance at the McKinnon Hotel was 23 Aug 2026, closing a ten-year run of 2,670 shows to some 700,000 visitors; listings had it booking to 30 Aug. Nothing comparable has been announced in its place. Also removed from Thursday's open-night note, where it held one of three standing suggestions.

events.title: Fotografiska Wednesday Jazz
events.blurb: Foto Live jazz-and-cocktails on the 4F lounge stage. The 28th is now your working day, which makes an evening that needs no planning and no walking worth knowing about. You did Fotografiska itself in April; the jazz night is the new part.

events.title: Jota Mombaça: stuck in movement (in the tide)
events.blurb: Three shows open together on the 22nd: Mombaça's fragmented, planetary-grief opera anchors the museum alongside Kandis Williams' collage piece A Cave and Wong Kit Yi's karaoke-themed companion work. On the Bund, a short hop from People's Square.

events.title: China Shanghai International Arts Festival
events.blurb: The 25th edition runs 17 Oct to 15 Nov: around 400 programmes and 1,100 performances and exhibitions, with a main bill of 60 productions across 168 shows. Nearly 90 per cent are Shanghai premieres and thirteen play nowhere else in China. A good share is wordless or in English. The individual shows landing in your ten days are listed separately below rather than left inside this entry; the festival's own calendar at artsbird.com/en/calendar/2026-10 is the place to check for late additions.

events.title: Stratovarius
events.blurb: Finnish power-metal veterans, in town on Halloween night of all nights. Not remotely jazz — but it's the one dated gig on your Saturday so far, and MAO on a costume night would be a scene.
events.hiddenNote: Not wanted. Halloween at MAO is a fine scene and the wrong one for this week's last night, which is the crab and then the Old Jazz Band.

events.title: French Concession, on foot
events.blurb: English-guided walks through the plane-tree streets — the Wukang Building, the shikumen lanes, the Art Deco that Shanghai wears more casually than anywhere else. Historic Shanghai and several operators run them, with private departures bookable for any morning or afternoon, so pin it to a day with a gap.

events.title: Yangpu Flea Market
events.blurb: Old cameras, Mao-era pins, cultural-revolution ephemera and honest junk, traded from dawn to about noon three mornings a week. No English needed and none offered; it sits near the Saturday's Yangpu riverfront, so an early start folds it in.

events.title: Kung Fu Komedy
events.blurb: China's first stand-up room, English and Chinese acts on rotation, with free open mics on the quieter nights — email a day ahead to get on the list, or just watch. Small, solo-friendly, and the most reliable English-language laugh in town.
events.archiveNote: The venue's own SmartShanghai listing now reads "This venue has closed." No replacement English-language stand-up room has been confirmed yet — Comedy UN (a Kung Fu Komedy alum's newer club) turned up several conflicting/stale addresses across sources, so nothing solid enough to add in its place this run.

events.title: JZ Club
events.blurb: The city's serious jazz room, two sets most nights, touring names dropped in among the residents. No language barrier and no need to give up a whole evening — a late set after dinner does it.

events.title: Tosca — Teatro La Fenice
events.venue: Shanghai Grand Opera House · Harmony Hall
events.blurb: Teatro La Fenice's own production, its Asian premiere, in the new opera house's 2,000-seat Harmony Hall — part of the venue's opening season, on your Saturday. Sung in Italian; the other of its two Shanghai dates is the 22nd, before you land.

events.title: Aida — Mariinsky Theatre
events.venue: Shanghai Grand Opera House · Harmony Hall
events.blurb: Valery Gergiev conducts the Mariinsky's own production — nearly 300 cast and crew touring in for the new house's opening season, running your last Friday through the day you fly out. Sung in Italian.

events.title: Shostakovich Symphony Cycle — Mariinsky Orchestra
events.blurb: Valery Gergiev leads the Mariinsky Orchestra through all fifteen Shostakovich symphonies over six nights, marking the composer's 120th birthday and part of the new opera house's opening season alongside Tosca and Aida down the hall. Purely orchestral — nothing to translate.

events.title: Ballet Essentials — Moscow Grand Theatre Ballet
events.blurb: Two performances of highlights from the touring company's ballet repertoire; one date carries an afternoon matinee slot, though the venue listing doesn't specify which. Visual storytelling, nothing to translate.

events.title: Andrea Bocelli — Romanza 30th Anniversary Tour
events.blurb: Bocelli's 30th-anniversary tour lands on Halloween night — the arena option if Stratovarius at MAO Livehouse isn't your thing. Sung mostly in Italian; a concert, not a conversation, so language isn't really the point either way.
events.hiddenNote: Not wanted. Arena scale on the night the week ends at a twenty-seat counter and a bar in the 1929 Cathay.

events.title: JOYCE — "Talent for Peach Blossoms" Tour
events.blurb: Taiwanese singer-songwriter JOYCE plays a solo date on her 2026 tour, the same evening as Tosca across town. Mandarin-language pop — fine as a gig, but don't expect to follow the lyrics.

events.title: Moby Dick — Robert Wilson & Düsseldorfer Schauspielhaus
events.blurb: Robert Wilson's last fully directed production, and its first showing in China: Melville staged as slow-motion tableau, with songs by Anna Calvi. German with surtitles, which matters less than usual here — Wilson's theatre is built to be looked at. The catch is the calendar: the 24th is landing day and Saturday ends at eight, and the 25th is the Lost Plate tour. Part of the Dance Reflections strand inside the arts festival.

events.title: Save the Last Dance for Me — Alessandro Sciarroni
events.venue: Power Station of Art (28th) · West Bund Museum (29th)
events.blurb: Sciarroni reconstructs Polka Chinata, a near-extinct Bolognese courtship dance for two men who grip each other and spin while folding to the floor. Roughly half an hour, wordless. On the page for Thursday the 29th at West Bund Museum, 2pm, because the 28th, at Power Station of Art, is the day that starts at twenty to three. The 28th books through Power Station of Art; nothing is published for booking the 29th yet.

events.title: He Who Falls — Yoann Bourgeois Art Company
events.blurb: Six people try to stay upright on a suspended platform that spins, tilts and drops. Wordless, about an hour, and one of the few pieces of contemporary circus that earns the word. Now Friday's evening on the page, at 1650 Hongqiao Rd; the 31st is the crab. The festival calendar has the curtain at 7:30 on both nights.

events.title: Trisha Brown: In Plain Site
events.blurb: The company's site-specific format: Brown's repertory re-set into whatever building it lands in, rather than onto a stage. Wordless, usually short, and the Shanghai venue is the point of it — worth checking where they put it. The 1 Nov date is the flight home.
events.hiddenNote: Not wanted. Would have cost Saturday's crab and the Old Jazz Band, and the venue and curtain were never published.

events.title: Numerical Series 15 | 18 — TAO Dance Theater
events.blurb: Tao Ye's company counts its works by the number of bodies in them. Pure movement, no narrative, no language, and a Chinese contemporary company with a genuine international standing rather than a local one.
events.hiddenNote: Not wanted, same night and same cost as the Trisha Brown. Sciarroni on the 29th and Bourgeois on the 30th are the dance this week carries.

events.title: Contre-Nature — Rachid Ouramdane / Compagnie de Chaillot
events.blurb: Contemporary dance with aerial work, from the director of Paris's Chaillot. Wordless. Both dates are awkward — the 24th is landing day, the 25th is the food tour — so this is here for completeness rather than as a real candidate.

events.title: The Starry Nights — Argerich, Vengerov, Isserlis and friends
events.blurb: Martha Argerich, Maxim Vengerov and Steven Isserlis playing chamber music on two consecutive nights. The 24th is Liszt, Schumann, Mahler and Beethoven; the 25th is Shostakovich, Beethoven, Kreisler and Ravel. Argerich is 85 and does not tour much. Both nights clash with the page as it stands, which is exactly the sort of thing worth knowing early.
events.hiddenNote: Not wanted. The 25th is the Lost Plate tour, kept over this, and the 24th is landing day.

events.title: Hamlet — Beijing People's Art Theatre
events.blurb: A new main-stage Hamlet from China's most prestigious drama company, co-directed by Feng Yuanzheng, in the 1941 Majestic on Jiangning Rd. Performed in Mandarin and long, so it asks more of you than the wordless work does; the building and the company are the reasons to consider it anyway.

events.title: Min Opera: Mr. Painted Hairnet
events.venue: Fujian Provincial Experimental Min Opera Theatre / CSIAF
events.blurb: Min opera is the regional form of Fuzhou, sung in Eastern Min rather than Mandarin, and it travels out of Fujian rarely. Subtitled in Chinese only, most likely. Here because it is the least exportable thing in the festival and it lands on a Tuesday that currently ends at half past seven.

events.title: Giorgio Morandi. Solo
events.blurb: The largest Morandi exhibition anywhere this century: 140-odd originals, over 120 shown in China for the first time, with the Museo Morandi in Bologna. Read the date carefully — it closes on the 28th, and the Pudong day on this page is the 29th. It is a five-minute walk from the Shanghai Museum East stop, on any day except that one.

events.title: Lina Bo Bardi: The Poetics of Survival
events.blurb: Bo Bardi's first exhibition in China, staged by OPEN Architecture, who have rebuilt the indoor pond from SESC Pompéia in the PSA lobby at full size. Closes on the 25th, so Saturday or Sunday or not at all. PSA is the old power station on the same bank between the Bund and West Bund, which makes Sunday the day it fits.

events.title: We Deem We Dream — Estelle Hanania
events.blurb: Photography by Estelle Hanania, who has spent years shooting European folk ritual and the dancers of Pina Bausch's company. Runs the whole trip, so it is the one in this batch with no timing problem at all.

events.title: X-TRA Digital Art Project: Terra Nova
events.blurb: The festival's digital-art commission, opening on the Friday of the trip and running into January. Opening weekends are the worst time to see anything, which is the only argument against it.

events.title: Creation — Pictures for Dorian
events.blurb: A Dorian Gray reworking at Theatre YOUNG, opening on the Friday; Friday's evening on this page is already He Who Falls. Language unconfirmed — worth checking before booking.

events.title: Le Roi Soleil — French musical
events.blurb: The Louis XIV pop-musical, sung in French with Chinese surtitles, opening on the Friday. Shanghai Culture Square is the sunken 2,000-seat house south of Huaihai Rd. Big, unsubtle and entirely singable-along if that is the evening you want.

events.title: ERA2 — Spirit of Shanghai
events.blurb: The long-running acrobatics spectacular, rebuilt as a second edition. Wordless by definition and runs most nights, so it is the reliable fallback rather than the event — useful to know exists on a night when nothing else lands.

events.title: Weekly Jam Night
events.blurb: An open jam on the one night of the week when most of the city's music rooms are dark. Monday the 26th currently ends with delivery in the room; this is the low-commitment alternative if it stops too hard.
